context.why: Stories 1 and 2 are accepted: Contribution.level, RecordAccess, Crediting (add with an organization, update, remove, credited_from) and the tab's list, portal add, edit and remove pages are rebuilt and tested, with the organization choice behind AffiliationChoice. This story rebuilds the other two ways of adding a contributor, on both add pages (add-person and add-organization): looking them up in a registry (ORCID for a person, ROR for an organization) and entering them by hand. The maintainer approved the pages as the prototype draws them (templates contributors/plugins/contribution_add_person.html and contribution_add_organization.html): three stock radio tabs that switch in the browser, a search that redraws only its own tab through htmx (hx-get with hx-select on #tab-portal / #tab-registry / #tab-new), a 'searching' indicator, results, a no-result state, a chosen step, and the by-hand form with a same-name warning. Behind them the prototype uses fixed ORCID_RECORDS and ROR_RECORDS lists and a time.sleep pause in plugins/shared.py; this story replaces those with real calls and deletes them.

prior_decisions: decisions.md D5: `Orcid` and `Ror` are two plain classes in fairdm/contrib/contributors/services/registries.py with no shared base class. A small module-level helper for the HTTP call and its failure handling is fine. RegistryUnavailable is the one exception both raise.

Real responses are recorded under specs/022-record-contributors-and-access/recorded/ (orcid-search.json, orcid-search-by-id.json, orcid-record.json, ror-search.json, ror-record.json, ror-missing.json which is a 404 body). Build your test doubles from them: copy trimmed pieces into your test module or a fixture file under tests/, do not read from specs/ at test time. Endpoints, all public and needing no credentials: ORCID search `https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/expanded-search/` with params q and rows and header Accept: application/json (search by iD with q=`orcid:<iD>`); ORCID fetch `https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/<iD>/record`; ROR search `https://api.ror.org/v2/organizations` with param query; ROR fetch `https://api.ror.org/v2/organizations/<id>`. An ORCID search result has given-names, family-names, orcid-id, institution-name (a list; the first is the employer shown and suggested). A ROR item has id (a full https://ror.org/ URL), names (take the one whose types include ror_display), types, status (leave out anything not active), locations[].geonames_details (name, country_name).
Replace the network at `requests.get` (monkeypatch or unittest.mock); no test reaches the network and no new test dependency is added.

Security (plan D4): fetch refuses an identifier that does not match the registry's format before any request is made (reuse the ORCID pattern in models.py near Person and the ROR cleaner in utils/transforms.py); search terms go through requests' `params`, never string-formatted into the address; timeout five seconds; any network error, timeout or non-200 raises RegistryUnavailable. When a manager adds a chosen registry record, the page posts only the identifier and the server fetches the record again by that identifier before making a profile: never build a profile from posted name fields.

profile(record) returns the contributor the portal already holds under that identifier (ContributorIdentifier, type ORCID or ROR) or makes one with the name and the identifier. A person made this way has no email, an unusable password and no account. The prototype matched by name; that goes.

By hand: a person needs a given name and a family name, and may have an email address, which is stored and never shown; a person whose name matches profiles already in the portal gets those offered first and can still be made (the form comes back with a `confirmed` field); an organization needs a name and may have city, country and website, and when its name matches one in the portal the existing one is offered and no second is made. Person.email is unique: an address the portal already holds is refused on the email field with a code, and the response must not name, link or offer the profile it belongs to (it would let a manager find out who owns an address). The stored email must not make the person able to sign in or receive mail: check how Person and allauth treat a person with an email and an unusable password (PersonQuerySet state filters, AccountState.INVITED) and say in your report what state such a person is in.

Country on Organization is a django-countries field; the prototype's form takes free text. Offer the country as a choice from the field's own list in the form (a select) only if that does not change what the approved page draws beyond the input becoming a select; otherwise accept a country name or code and refuse what does not resolve. Say which you did in decisions.md.

FR-012: moving between the three ways must not reload the page or lose what another way holds. The templates already do this with radio tabs and htmx. Test what a test can decide: one response carries all three ways (scenario 1); a search response reopens on the way named by `via` in the address or the form (3); each tab keeps its own search term (`q` for the portal, `rq` for the registry). Do not test the browser behaviour.

FR-014: results are limited and the page says when there are more than it shows. The portal search and both registry searches need that flag in the context and one line in the template where the results end; that line is new text in an approved template, so keep it to one plain sentence in the same style as the 'no results' line beside it and name it in progress.md.
FR-015: when a registry cannot be reached the page answers 200, says that search is unavailable in the registry tab, and the other two ways still work. Same rule for new text in the template.
Every way of adding a person ends on the organization choice (AffiliationChoice, story 2) and goes through Crediting.add; then the manager is sent to the new contributor's edit page (FR-020).
decisions.md D7: a superuser is refused by Crediting.add with a ValidationError.

Docs: the names this story makes public must be documented (T014). The four names the docs step already reports belong to later stories: ContributionMove and level_choices (plugins/shared.py), give_level (demo/seed/common.py), ContributorSeed (demo/seed/contributors.py).

acceptance.given_when_then: Given replaced responses built from the recorded ones, when Orcid and Ror search, fetch and make a profile, then the outcomes in tasks.md T011 hold, a malformed identifier makes no request, and every failure raises RegistryUnavailable.

Given User Story 3's scenarios, when both add pages are used through the test client by a manager, a reader and a visitor, then each Then holds, a registry that cannot be reached still answers 200 with the other ways working, and nothing is made by someone who may not manage the record.
Given the failing tests from T011 and T012, when the implementation lands, then all pass and the fixed records and the pause are gone from plugins/shared.py.

Given the user, administrator and developer pages named in tasks.md T014, when read against the branch, then they describe the three ways, what the portal needs to reach ORCID and ROR and what happens when it cannot, and the registry classes.
